date_note: Date of the attack as given in the company's notice relayed by Daily Security; the company posted its notice on Nov 25.
title: Token Post (Korea) says an attacker took over an admin account and some member data leaked
summary: According to a notice Token Post posted on Nov 25, relayed by Daily Security, an external attacker took over an admin account on Nov 21 and looked up some members' data. Leaked items vary by member and include nicknames, emails, wallet addresses, some real names and NEWS token trade history. The company says passwords are encrypted and it has found no sign of password leakage.
plain: A Korean crypto news site says an attacker got into an admin account and some members' details, such as emails and wallet addresses, were exposed. It says passwords are encrypted and no leak of them was found.
exec: Wallet addresses combined with names and emails can enable targeted phishing of crypto users, according to the Daily Security reporter.
action: Token Post advises members to change passwords, enable two-factor authentication and ignore messages impersonating Token Post that ask for passwords, keys or transfers.

validation.note: Only Daily Security read, relaying Token Post's own Nov 25 notice; the notice itself was not opened.

review.note: attack date, notice, leaked items, password statement, advice checked against Daily Security
